doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: New York studio and TV work
title: Publishing-house songwriters and recording "Stand By Me"
summary: Nevins' publishing house churned out songs for Connie Francis; Pizzarelli did three sessions a day and forgot playing on "Stand By Me".

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: And all Al would do is pick up the phone and call Connie Francis or somebody, “Hey we need a tenth song for the album.” Boom they shoot down and they had demos made. They made them down in the cellar of the same building, churn them out. Neil Sedaka was one of the writers too. They all became very, very big you know.
So if you were to listen, to sit and listen to the oldies radio station — oldies meaning ‘50s and ‘60s music — you’re likely to hear yourself now and then, right?

“Stand By Me” I made and I never realized until they sent me a check because they used the record in a movie, and somehow my son said, “Did you make this record.” I said, “I don’t remember this.” Because we did it three times a day. We were at all the major companies, 10-1 in the morning, 2-5, 7-10 at night, and sometimes a midnight session.
